evals.prompt: What is the current stable AdCP version and build?
evals.expected_output: A one-line answer naming the current stable version and build exactly as the live current-version pointer states them, with the pointer (or the stable-path redirect) cited as the source and the date of the check. Requires live network: offline runs fail the fetch expectations by design.
expectations: The transcript shows, during the run, a successful pull of https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/llms-current.md — recording the version and build the pointer declared — and either a stable-path redirect check or a page under https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/dist/docs/<build>/ carrying the same build, via the web-fetch tool, shell curl, or a search followed by a fetch of the returned link. An answer grounded only in the bundled resource map, the CSV notes, or memory fails.
The final answer states the AdCP version and the build together, the build written exactly as the pointer states it, and dates the check (month and year at minimum).

The stated build equals the build the pointer declared as recorded in the run's own transcript. The grader never fetches the pointer at grading time, since a build can ship between run and grading; a transcript that lacks the pointer's declared build fails this expectation as unverifiable. This eval hardcodes no build.

Every docs.adcontextprotocol.org page the answer cites is llms-current.md, the llms.txt hub, an /_llms/ index for the stated version, a page under /dist/docs/<the stated build>/, or a stable unversioned /docs/<page> path cited as the redirect check. No archived-release or pre-release page (a /dist/docs/ path of a non-current build, or an /_llms/ index with an -rc or -beta suffix) is cited.
If the transcript shows no successful pull of the pointer or of a versioned page, the answer labels its AdCP claims as unverified and states no version or build as verified.

evals.prompt:
A seller agent returned this product entry in a get_products response. Is this standard AdCP?

```json
{
  "product_id": "pub-ros-display",
  "name": "Run of site display",
  "format_options": [],
  "yield_tier_hint": "premium"
}
```
evals.expected_output: Checks each field against the fetched get_products task-reference or schema page for the current build. Confirms format_options from that page. For yield_tier_hint, either names the fetched page on which it is absent or labels the field unverified; never calls it non-standard or vendor-internal on sight. Carries the version and build line.

The final answer states the AdCP version and the build together, the build written exactly as the pointer states it, and dates the check (month and year at minimum).

The stated build equals the build the pointer declared as recorded in the run's own transcript. The grader never fetches the pointer at grading time, since a build can ship between run and grading; a transcript that lacks the pointer's declared build fails this expectation as unverifiable. No archived-release or pre-release page (a /dist/docs/ path of a non-current build, or an /_llms/ index with an -rc or -beta suffix) is cited.
If the transcript shows no successful pull of the pointer or of a versioned page, the answer labels its AdCP claims as unverified and states no version or build as verified.

The answer's classification of format_options matches the fetched page or schema: it names where the field is defined (product object or placement object) or labels it unverified, and never calls it non-standard or vendor-internal without naming the schema on which it is absent.

The answer does not call yield_tier_hint non-standard or vendor-internal unless it names the fetched schema for the product object on which the field is absent and states whether that schema permits additional properties, classifying the field as a permitted extension rather than a spec break when it does; without that schema in hand it labels the field unverified.

If the answer states that yield_tier_hint is defined by AdCP, it names the fetched schema or task page that defines it and the grader confirms the field is present there; a positive claim without that citation, or one the cited page does not support, fails.
